lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, everyone's here. This is the Hawker Heroes launch-readiness check. Four items today: build and bugs, level 5 difficulty, the publisher milestone, then launch marketing and the booth budget.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Arjun, let's start with the build. Where are we?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Release candidate two went out to the testers on Monday. Frame rate is fine on the mid-range Android phones now, the memory fix from last week worked.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: The big one is still the crash. If you serve ten customers in a row without a break, the game crashes. It happens on every device we tried.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: That's the rush hour in the satay stall level, so most players will hit it in the first twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: That blocks the launch build then. Arjun, can you get a proper bug ticket filed for the ten-customer crash so it's tracked, with the repro steps?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Yes, I'll file it today. I think it's the order queue not being cleared, but I need to confirm with a debug build.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Other than that, two minor bugs: the pause menu text overlaps on small screens, and the tutorial skip button sometimes needs two taps. Both are small and I'll fix them in this sprint.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Can the tutorial skip go in before the playtest on Friday? Testers keep complaining about it.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Should be fine, it's a one-line change.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Good. Anything else on the build? Store screenshots, crash reporting?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Crash reporting is on in the release candidate, so we'll see real numbers from the testers by Thursday.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Do the screenshots need the new UI?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Yes, take them from release candidate two, the old UI is gone.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Great, that's build and bugs. Let's move on to level 5 difficulty and the playtest feedback. Mei, over to you.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: So, the playtest. Fourteen of the twenty playtesters quit on level 5. That's the big drop-off, everything before it is fine.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Level 5 is where the second stall opens and you have to cook and serve at the same time. People said it felt unfair, not hard.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Is it the timer? We cut the customer patience timer in that level by thirty percent.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Maybe. I want to try putting the patience back and adding a tutorial pop-up for the second stall.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Do we know exactly where in level 5 players quit? Is it the first rush, or the second stall, or the end?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Honestly I don't have the breakdown with me. The playtest sheet has per-wave numbers but I haven't looked at it since last week.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I could add analytics events per wave, but that won't be in before launch.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Some testers also wanted the soundtrack quieter during the rush, it's stressful. That's an easy change.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Let's not redesign the whole level. What's the smallest change that gets people through it?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Patience timer back to normal, plus the pop-up. I can have both ready for Friday's playtest.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: The pop-up needs a new tutorial step, so it's half a day for me. The timer is just a config value.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Then let's do the timer first and see how Friday goes before we spend the half day.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Agreed. I'd rather spend the time on the crash.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: One more thing on level 5, the stall upgrade prices. Players said they never had enough coins by then.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Let's take the coin balance offline, we're over time on this one. Moving on to the publisher milestone.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Starfruit wants a milestone report and the final build. The report is mostly done, I'll send it to them this week.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: When does Starfruit need the final build? That decides whether the crash fix makes it.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: The wiki says the twenty-fifth of November, but I remember an email from them saying earlier. I don't want to guess.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: If it's earlier than the twentieth, we're tight.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: The milestone payment is tied to the report, not the build, so that part is fine either way.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Do they need the store page text from us too, or do they write it?

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: We write it, they review it. I'll draft it with Daniel.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: And once the final build date is confirmed, I'll post the launch date in the team channel so everyone works to the same date.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Please do, half the team still thinks it's December.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, last item: launch marketing and the booth budget.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Indie Arcade SG confirmed our booth. The budget we agreed was two thousand dollars, and we've already spent most of it on the banner and the stand.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Can we still get the two demo tablets? Visitors should play the satay level, not watch a trailer.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: If we borrow tablets from the office we save about four hundred.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: For the launch itself, the marketing plan still has no live stream. Every cozy game that did well this year had a streamer play it on day one.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Daniel, can you email a streamer and ask them to play Hawker Heroes on launch day? Someone who does cozy and cooking games.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Sure, I'll email one.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: We could also give out stickers at the booth, the hawker uncle ones are really popular with the testers.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Stickers are cheap, let's do it if there's budget left after the tablets.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Will the booth build be the release build? I'd rather not demo a build that crashes after ten customers.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Good point, the booth gets whatever has the crash fix.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: That's everything. Thanks all, good meeting.
